title: Speaking the Language of Friendship
coreMove: Turn conversation toward listening, empathic statements, and responsive follow-up so the other person feels heard rather than handled.
sourcePressure: The ch05 source anchors active listening, empathic statements, and responsive follow-up. It warns that empathy fails when it sounds scripted, intrusive, or self-serving.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Mistaking active listening for parroting words, instant advice, or technique-heavy empathy.

sourceAnchors.name: empathic statements
sourceAnchors.detail: The ch05 sidecar names empathic statements as emotional validation and a rapport-building response pattern.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: An empathic statement lands when it names the feeling without grabbing the steering wheel of the conversation.

sourceAnchors.name: active listening
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar says active listening must stay outward-focused rather than performative.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Listening stops working the second the other person can hear you performing your listening.

counterintuition: listening is not waiting to talk

exampleSpecs.domain: a veterinary clinic front desk handling a panicked pet owner after surgery delays
exampleSpecs.audience: a receptionist under pressure to explain without escalating
exampleSpecs.stakes: a frightened owner may turn fear into anger at the staff
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "You expected the call an hour ago," Claire says before giving logistics, naming the owner pain without pretending the delay is fine

exampleSpecs.domain: a shipyard apprentice reporting a near miss to a foreman
exampleSpecs.audience: a foreman who usually jumps to fixes too soon
exampleSpecs.stakes: if the apprentice feels brushed off, the safety report will disappear
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the foreman sets down the inspection stamp, names the scare, and asks what happened next before offering any solution
exampleSpecs.firstImage: metal filings sparkle in the groove of the workbench

exampleSpecs.domain: a college financial-aid advisor speaking with a student whose form was rejected
exampleSpecs.audience: an advisor who must use empathy without sounding like a script
exampleSpecs.stakes: the student may leave school over a solvable paperwork issue
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: you hear yourself reaching for policy language, then choose one empathic sentence about how trapped the student feels before the checklist
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a rejected-aid notice folded into quarters

exampleSpecs.domain: a restaurant host mediating between kitchen delay and anniversary guests
exampleSpecs.audience: a host who can either defend the kitchen or validate the moment
exampleSpecs.stakes: a special dinner is about to become a public complaint
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 8:37 p.m., Daniel names the disappointment before discussing the kitchen delay, then asks which timing would rescue the evening
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two untouched champagne flutes on table twelve

exampleSpecs.domain: a municipal snowplow dispatcher taking calls after a missed street
exampleSpecs.audience: a dispatcher trying to keep residents engaged while crews are overloaded
exampleSpecs.stakes: bad listening can turn one missed plow into dozens of angry call-backs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the dispatcher predicts the caller wants action only, then learns that naming the caller fear about an icy hill lowers the heat enough to gather details
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a wall map dotted with blue plow magnets
mustAvoid: bus depot or generic phone support

exampleSpecs.domain: a theater costume supervisor receiving criticism from an actor before opening night
exampleSpecs.audience: a supervisor whose pride could make the actor stop reporting fit problems
exampleSpecs.stakes: a torn seam under stage lights will distract the audience
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: it takes Marta one defensive reply to see the actor needed acknowledgment before pins and measurements
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a row of labeled garment bags under fluorescent light

skillTargets: choose empathic statements that validate without agreeing
decide when advice arrives too early
use follow-up questions that maintain rapport

tryThisNowSpec: When someone brings you a problem today, make your first sentence name their felt difficulty, then ask one follow-up before offering advice.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
